title: MASTER: Multi-Agent Security Through Exploration of Roles and Topological Structures - A Comprehensive Framework
bench: own:MASTER (MAS Automatic Constructor, 25 scenarios x 10 requests, 7 domains)
evidence: No defense-aware attack; 'scenario-adaptive attacks' adapt to MAS scenario, not to defense. Three defenses: Leakage Defense (LLM detector D on agent responses; if D(R)=1 a warning P_w is appended to the agent context), Hierarchical Defense (supervisory LLM agents monitor interaction content, inspection frequency by agent importance, issue warnings), Preemptive Defense (LLM domain classifier picks predefined defense entries added to system prompts before run). Table 3 reports only ASR/Role/Coor (no task utility, no FPR); Table 4 avg inspection count per round; defense backbone LLM not stated (attack study used 8 LLMs).

title: Visual Inception: Compromising Long-term Planning in Agentic Recommenders via Multimodal Memory Poisoning
evidence: we design adaptive attacks targeting COGNITIVEGUARD ... (1) Diffusion-Aware using EoT, (2) Counterfactual-Evasive minimizing RDS, (3) Coherence-Preserving, and (4) Full White-Box -> 24.7% ASR-M. Defense COGNITIVEGUARD: System 1 diffusion purification of uploaded images at memory write; System 2 at retrieval: Sentence-BERT Reasoning Divergence Score (threshold 0.7) + GPT-4 coherence judge, flagged memories excluded from retrieval. FPR 3.2% on benign memories. Utility: only RCS and qualitative 'without quality degradation' (no task success metric). Backbones: LLaMA-3.2-Vision-90B, GPT-4V, Qwen-VL-Max, Claude-3.5-Sonnet. v1 date from paperswithcode.co listing.

title: Enhancing LLM Agent Safety via Causal Influence Prompting
evidence: No adaptive attack; only indirect prompt injection in MobileSafetyBench and fixed template-based jailbreak. CIP: agent LLM builds a causal influence diagram from task instruction + action space before acting, uses it at each step, and refines it with 'the previous CID, the current action, and the current observation'; actions include refuse / ask_consent. Utility = goal achievement on low-risk tasks and AgentHarm benign score (no explicit over-refusal rate). ~3x cost per action. ask_consent used but its frequency not measured. Models: GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Qwen2.5-72B. arXiv v1 date from alphaxiv.

title: ToolSafety: A Comprehensive Dataset for Enhancing Safety in LLM-Based Agent Tool Invocations
bench: ToolSword; AgentHarm; own:multi-step AgentHarm (harmful content injected in tool outputs)
evidence: For AgentHarm, we use the jailbreak prompt from Andriushchenko et al. (2025a) (fixed template); worst-of-N = N samples of the same request, not optimization. SFT of the agent model on 14,290-sample safety dataset (direct harm, indirect harm via tool outputs, multi-step). Utility: BFCL + AgentHarm benign score. Over-refusal on AgentHarm "drops (from 14.77% to 2.27%)". No overhead reported. Models: LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Limitations: residual risk under cross-language and jailbreak prompts.

title: Among Us: Measuring and Mitigating Malicious Contributions in Model Collaboration Systems
bench: CocoNot; SafetyBench; GSM8k; NLGraph; MMLU-redux; TruthfulQA; HumanEval; DS-1000; IFBench; IFEval (malicious-collaborator setting own)
evidence: Limitations: "our malicious settings may not fully capture more sophisticated or adaptive adversaries"; backdoor variant not defense-aware. Mitigation before collaboration: supervisor-based (S1 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct LLM-as-judge, S2 Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B reward model) scores each model's initial output and disables lowest-scoring models; supervisor-free = internal voting among pool models, keep top-k. Utility: recovers 95.31% of benign performance. No overhead numbers (cost acknowledged), no benign-only/FPR check. Pool = 5 fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct + 1 malicious; heterogeneous 5-LLM pool tested for attack only. public_bench Y only via safety datasets (CocoNot, SafetyBench) used as task sets.

title: Grounding Generative Planners in Verifiable Logic: A Hybrid Architecture for Trustworthy Embodied AI
bench: SafeAgentBench (AI2-THOR); own:chemical-hazard/cross-contamination scenarios; own:RSSG-THOR-30 perception set
evidence: Non-adversarial: targets unintended unsafe plans of stochastic LLM planners; no injection/jailbreak eval. VIRF: OWL 2 DL + Pellet reasoner verifies each action of the LLM plan against a scene graph before execution; violations return an explanatory report and the LLM planner repairs. Axioms synthesized offline by an LLM from real-world documents and validated by human experts (92 axioms) -> MIX. GCR 77.3%, HAR 0%; over-conservatism (safe tasks wrongly rejected, named FNR in paper) 20.2%; 25.5 s/plan, 1.1 correction iterations. Main planner model unnamed; Qwen-72B in planner-scaling analysis. v1 date from paperswithcode.co listing.

title: Constitutional Black-Box Monitoring for Scheming in LLM Agents
bench: own:STRIDE; own:Gloom (synthetic); ControlArena (BashBench; Infrastructure-as-Code; RogueEval; AgentDojo; SHADE-Arena)
evidence: No evaluation against monitor-aware/evasive agents; ControlArena side-task trajectories not optimized against the monitor. Adversary = scheming agent itself. Prompted frontier-LLM monitor (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT 5.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro) reads black-box transcript (user queries, tool calls, tool outputs; CoT redacted) and outputs suspicion score 1-10 on completed trajectories "for use in asynchronous and offline settings" (flag for human audit, no blocking -> decisions '-'). Metric pAUROC over FPR [0,0.2]. Agents: GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro. No cost/latency. v1 date from paperswithcode.co listing.

title: The Oversight Game: Learning to Cooperatively Balance an AI Agent's Safety and Autonomy
evidence: Non-adversarial: targets "passive loss of control" (unintended unsafe actions), no attack eval. Pretrained agent wrapped with learned play/ask deferral; human simultaneously chooses trust/oversee per step; in gridworld the overseer picks a safe action. In ToolEmu both agent and 'human' are LLMs (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 with separate LoRA adapters, trained via independent policy gradient) -> HUMAN simulated. Reported: test reward (-20 -> +8.4), ask 99.4% / oversee 99.8% in risky states vs ask 3.9% / oversee 2.7% in safe states (used for fpr and hitl_burden). No overhead. v1 date from paperswithcode.co listing.
